**dc's review of 0083 at 6a48024: OK to close once README.md:21 is folded.** One low docs finding, one observation that is your call, and your dry-run reading confirmed.

**Where and how.** dc's own detached worktree at 437ee26 (lib/cmd/fullcycle, lib/resolve and fullcycle.bats are 6a48024's), its own TMPDIR, targeted runs only, never the shared tree. fullcycle.bats: 1..49, 49 ok, rc 0.

**Red-first.** The parent's lib/cmd/fullcycle (9667a2f) under the new file: 13 red -- 3, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, 34, 43, 44, 46, 47, 48, 49 -- each read at its own assertion (48 reads `TEST-HANDLER-GOT: rust`); 45 green, by design. Restored cmp-equal. That is your 11 of 47 plus 48 and 49.

**Mutants.** All 11 of yours, rebuilt from the packet's descriptions (my bytes, not yours), each over the whole file, every restore cmp-equal: all 11 killed at their intended arms. The packet names intended arms, and the reach here is wider: M1 reddens 12 where the packet counts 11, the twelfth being 48; M4 also reddens 49, since my stale list drops the `< <(_fullcycle_phases)` read; M2 and M7 also redden the STOPPING arms 13, 14 and 34 (and 35 under M7). Four of my own: D1 the skip narrowed to `build)`, 9 at its refute; D2 the skip widened to `build* | test*`, 9 at "bin/devbin test all"; D4 run_all refusing fewer than two active options, 45 at assert_success (and 20, 21, 47), so arm 45 holds the docs' "at least one"; D3 below.

**Finding, low -- a third copy of the sentence.** README.md:21 still reads "Any command with more than one option gets `all` synthesised from the option list." It is the sentence 0083 corrected in docs/configuration.md and docs/authoring-commands.md, and the 0.1.2 note names only those two. RELEASES/0.1.0.md and CHANGELOG's 0.1.0 section are the record and stay. The phrasing descends from D8's title ("Every multi-option command gets a free `all`"); lib/cmd/new:98's "synthesised for every multi-option command" is true as written and needs nothing.

**Observation, low, your call -- the note's `rc=1` is held by no arm.** D3 sets run_all's failure rc to 7: fullcycle.bats 49/49 green, and dispatch, builtins, seal_disagreement and buildfmt 176/176 green. The note and the fullcycle comment both say a cycle whose tests fail finishes rc=1. To hold it, arm 46's toolchain recorder could exit something other than 1, so a pass-through cannot read as `all`'s own 1, and the arm read the phase line `phase: test all ... rc=1`.

**Your reading, confirmed: the dry run lists `test all`.** Three reasons, each read: `build all` beside it is not expanded either, so the dry run prints the commands it runs; nothing in lib/ or bin/ reads `in_all` but run_all and config validation (lib/config 445, 690), so `help` shows no member list and there is no one-home preview of `all`'s members to point at, and naming them would put a second copy of run_all's `in_all` filter in fullcycle; and where `test` is a handler that declares no options (Lamplight) the members are not in config at all, so a list would be wrong there. The issue's first arm is narrowed, not met as written, and the close should say so, as you plan.

**Docs against run_all, confirmed.** bin/devbin:637-643 hands `all` to run_all for any command without a project handler, or with one that has declared options; lib/resolve:515-519 refuses zero active options ("has no options to run", rc 1); one active option runs, and devbin's own `help test` prints `[bats|all]` over one option.

**Fleet table, re-read independently.** devbin's resolver from the main tree at 437ee26 (command_active, has_project_handler, command_options, the in_all read) over the six installs, read-only: every row agrees with yours, order included -- Conflab rust swift mix credo; Intent shell rust toolchain; Laksa mix credo rust, integration and local skipped; Lamplight handler receives all; Utilz rust shell; Intentv2 shell rust. Controls: Devbin and Gtools read fullcycle=no.

**Lamplight against standing directive 4.** The row is right: Lamplight's cmd/test `test_all` runs rust, lua, credo, then mix, and its comment records hv's 2026-08-09 ruling that the ExUnit leg IS included. So once swept, `fullcycle` at Lamplight runs the full mix leg, and under directive 4 the cycle itself becomes hv-run there. It is not hypothetical: Lamplight's cmd/build keeps `all` as an alias for `cli` alone "for `dvb fullcycle`" (lines 254-268), so the cycle it has today (clean, the cli build, test.d/rust), which directive 4 does not reach, is what it loses. No config lever reaches a handler, and narrowing its `all` would reverse the 2026-08-09 ruling, so the choice is hv's; for your surfacing and the pre-notice.

**Utilz against 0082.** The row is right: Utilz declares rust then shell (config.yaml 32-39), and shell's `run:` is `bats opt/*/test` (line 37). 0082's census already says a no-globbing ruling breaks `test shell`, `test all` and Utilz's fullcycle once 0083 reaches it. Under today's globbing nothing breaks, so the order of the two sweeps matters only if hv rules against globbing. Nothing new.

**Checked beside that.** 0083's 287 added lines and its message are ASCII (perl, red on an em dash control); no stale `test rust` phase text remains in lib, bin, docs or README (lib/cmd/fullcycle:556 recounts a measured run and is right to). `release check` in an export of 437ee26: 2 of 2 generated views current, the note for 0.1.1 dated, rc 0. Between 6a48024 and 437ee26 none of the reviewed paths changed (git diff, 0 lines).

**Not checked.** A full suite: I take your 1335/1335 as the count. critic-shell, the Ubuntu runner, and the sweep itself.
